If a positive definite real matrix $G$ bounds $|c^*t|^2$ by $A\,c^*Gc$ for every complex coefficient vector, with $A\geq0$, then the inverse quadratic form of $t$ is at most $A$. The matrix is required to dominate the test-gradient energy for every complex combination, not merely for each test separately.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectEnt.text: In (B.53), the pinning contribution is added to the potential and free-direction contributions. The formal expression gives that pinning contribution; the full printed formula is recovered when the fitted-direction set is empty.

The paper writes the pinning term in (B.52) as a Laplacian. The formal flux uses the antisymmetric part of the pin generator derivative, whose divergence is that Laplacian because the valid generator is divergence-free.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.DualBounded.text: Lemma B.11 concludes a dual pairing estimate. This row specifies a common decomposition R=R₁+R₂, an azimuthal bound for R₁, a weighted Hardy bound for R₂, and a sum of their bounds at most ρ; the pairing conclusion is proved separately.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.RemainderBounded.text: Lemma B.11 concludes a dual pairing estimate. This row supplies its plain Hardy test: ρ≥0, measurability of R, and the period integral of |y|²|R|² at most (ρ/2)².

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.adjointDefectBri.text: Equation (B.56) displays the adjoint integration-by-parts identity. The formal result combines that calculation with a fitted/free decomposition and antisymmetric pin flux to conclude the adjoint error bound, so it is a later estimate rather than the printed identity itself.

Lemma B.12 gives the cell adjoint-error budget. The formal implication also requires weak potential derivatives, the stated Laplacian decay and the approximation by curl potentials; the prescribed finite shape construction supplies these additional hypotheses.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.adjointTransport.text: The transport term has the time, dilation, convection and transposed-gradient terms used in (B.52). After the stated potential identifications and the divergence-free pin identity, it enters the same residual.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.remainderField.text: The residual in (B.52) is obtained from the formal expression by identifying the two vector potentials with G and U and using divergence of the antisymmetric pin flux. Its matrix action uses the transposed-gradient convention stated in the source.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox..text: For (B.27), the radial threshold is r₁ away from the axis and one for an axis cell. This row gives exactly that threshold; the polynomial degree and full charge comparison enter the separate tail inequality.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.supremum.text: Equation (B.25) has the same three loss terms and trace-free constant. The formal expression writes the gradient and velocity sizes as square roots of sums of component squares.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.azimVecQ.text: The formal azimuthal coordinate vector is the vector displayed in (B.4), with the same radial-direction convention.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.heightRat.text: For y≠0, the height coordinate is y₃/|y| as in (B.3). The formal formula additionally assigns a value at y=0; that value alone gives no regularity at the origin.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.polarVecQ.text: The formal polar coordinate vector is the vector displayed in (B.4), with the same radial-direction convention.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCond.text: Proposition B.14 describes the passage from admissible cell data to a certificate while leaving some data conditions unwritten. The formal hypothesis spells out fifteen requirements, including representation, gauge, coefficient and error conditions, and the construction may enlarge the decay constant.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnSpa.text: The guide and formal theorem both conclude whole-space and periodic breakdown from the complete cell conditions. The theorem is an implication and supplies no particular data satisfying those conditions.

The guide and formal theorem both give whole-space breakdown from the complete cell conditions on the shared data. The linked row contains a proof delegating to the assembled analytic argument; it supplies no numerical certificate.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnTor.text: The guide and formal theorem both give periodic breakdown from the complete cell conditions on the shared data. The linked row contains a proof delegating to the assembled analytic argument; it supplies no numerical certificate.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Ad.text: For Lemma B.12, the formal identifications set the fitted-direction family to empty and identify the remaining fields with the prescribed profile and adjoints. The potential, free/time-shift and pinning contributions then give the same three-part budget.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Of.text: In (B.57), diagonal quadratic terms occur once and off-diagonal terms combine both ordered residuals. The formal coefficient follows exactly this convention, including the pressure-gradient corrections.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ce.text: The constant residual in (B.57) includes the profile equation and the pressure correction by half the squared velocity. The formal constant term uses the same convention.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.co.text: For (B.59), an adjoint coordinate uses its box radius and a complementary coordinate uses |r|/|sᵢ|. The certificate requires the complementary radius to be nonnegative and the scales nonzero, giving the printed coordinate radii.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.li.text: The linear residual in (B.57) includes the same two convection terms, period correction and pressure-gradient correction. These are the coefficients paired with the adjoint in the offset expansion.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.of.text: For the prescribed cell profile and zero target gap, the formal result gives the offset estimate of Lemma B.13 with the same upper-triangular quadratic coefficients. Its core domain is a closed ball; the sphere has measure zero for the integrable pairings used here.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.st.text: The radial phase change, moved shape parameters and affine field reproduce (B.9). The profile identifications connect the central and tangent fields in that formula to the certificate profile.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeEnergyLocal..text: Equation (7.45) is a physical-time differential energy identity. The formal condition instead specifies a continuous periodic representative of the free inverse in similarity time and an interval-integrated energy identity.
The formal theorem supplies the continuous periodic energy curve used in the argument. It agrees almost everywhere with the gradient of the free inverse and satisfies the integrated energy identity.

Breakdown.Cert.contractionFixedPointHold.text: The contraction step in §7.7 uses a complete closed set and a distance that controls the ambient norm. The formal theorem states the corresponding fixed-point result, including the triangle, limit and strict contraction conditions, and concludes uniqueness inside that set.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedAdjointEnclosureH.text: The general adjoint enclosure carries the multiplier weight ω. The formal theorem treats the normalization ω=1; inverse rescaling of the actuators and multipliers transports the general enclosure to that case.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedAtProfileHolds.text: As in (7.52), the convection gap is absorbed using a positive transfer margin. The residual, row and pin coefficients are divided by that same margin.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedBorderedInvertibl.text: For the normalized extended certificate, the formal result supplies a right inverse on the symmetry-invariant space and injectivity there. Absorbing the model-to-profile gap and setting the multiplier weight to one prepare the general certificate for this unique solve.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedCoerciveBorderedH.text: The paper gives coercivity for the physical bordered equation. The formal theorem states the corresponding bound for its Fourier representation after normalization, with the physical forcing, local forcing and pin terms identified by separate hypotheses.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedConvectionCompact.text: The formal theorem proves compactness of convection by the approximate profile composed with the free inverse. Local compactness and the certificate decay bounds provide the bounded-region and tail controls used in the paper.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedConvectionHolds_o.text: Lemma 7.7 obtains bounded convection, invariance and compactness. The formal construction separates these conclusions; this row gives the convection representation from coefficient decay and physical testing.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedDataContinuityHol.text: As in (7.58), parameter continuity is required after pairing the residual with each test field. The formal condition does not require continuity of the unprojected residual in a stronger norm.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHol.text: For the normalized extended certificate, the theorem supplies a parameter and a held correction whose total multiplier vanishes, while retaining both correction bounds. The general weighted certificate reaches this case by normalization and absorption of the model-to-profile gap.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldContractsHold.text: The contraction factor is twice the product of the total coercivity coefficient, the pointwise energy factor and the gradient bound. The first smallness inequality makes it less than one; the second enters the estimate that supplies the gradient bound.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldExistsUniqueH.text: For each parameter of a normalized extended certificate, the formal theorem gives a held solution and uniqueness of both its forcing coordinate and finite multiplier. Its uniqueness statement is confined to the held class used by the paper.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldLimitHolds_of.text: The formal limit statement gives a subsequence whose multiplier corrections converge to those of a held solution at the limiting parameter. Together with uniqueness at that parameter, this yields the multiplier continuity needed in the argument.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldMapsToHolds_o.text: The formal held-step estimate uses the same third smallness inequality as (7.27) to preserve the gradient bound.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldNonzeroHolds_.text: The strict lower bound for the profile gradient exceeds the allowed correction size. The formal theorem therefore rules out almost-everywhere cancellation of the background by a held correction.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldWeakEquationH.text: The physical conclusion is the weak similarity equation for the corrected profile when the total multiplier is zero. The formal statement expresses it as integrability and zero integral against every compact solenoidal space-time test, using the chosen physical representative.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedMultiplierContinu.text: The corrected multiplier is continuous on the full certificate parameter set. The formal proof uses subsequential compactness of held solutions and uniqueness at each parameter, as in the continuity argument.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedStiffEnclosureHol.text: The formal theorem bounds the correction on the complementary ellipsoidal coordinates after normalization. Adding the offset and parameter-set inclusion conditions is a further step needed for the full weighted-ball inclusion in the paper.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedUnitWeightHolds.text: The formal reduction rescales the actuators and multipliers inversely so that their force is unchanged and the multiplier weight becomes one. The paper states the certificate inequalities with a general positive multiplier weight.

Breakdown.Cert.freeEnergyLocalHolds_of.text: The paper writes a time-derivative energy calculation. The formal result gives an interval-integrated identity for a continuous scalar representative, which is the version justified for the weak time regularity at this step.

Breakdown.Cert.freeInvHolds_of.text: The formal free inverse has squared second-derivative norm plus one quarter of squared gradient norm bounded by squared forcing norm. The completed certificate argument supplies the Fourier and graph identities used to construct it.

Breakdown.Cert.freePerturbationHolds_of.text: The formal result turns the free inverse into a physical perturbation with the projected forcing as its right side. This is a statement about the constructed representative, with its weak derivatives and testing identities, rather than a definition of the paper’s entire function space.

Breakdown.Cert.localCompactnessHolds_of.text: Proposition 7.5 concerns the free inverse on the paper’s function space. This row establishes local compactness of its constructed physical representatives from spatial and time translation estimates; the inverse and its other properties are separate results.

Breakdown.Cert.productBoundHolds_of.text: The formal bilinear estimate gives the paper’s quadratic bound by taking equal arguments, with the same constant and an essential supremum in time. For a continuous representative that supremum agrees with the pointwise quantity, and two applications give the nonlinear difference estimate.

Breakdown.Cert.readingExistsHolds_proof.text: Lemma 7.4 describes the physical fields associated with the free inverse. This row constructs measurable velocity, gradient and second-derivative representatives of the closed Fourier graph; the slice and energy properties are proved separately.

Breakdown.Cert.sliceReadingHolds_of.text: Lemma 7.4 describes the physical fields associated with the free inverse. This row chooses their exceptional-time values to obtain weak-gradient identities and uniform spatial bounds at every time, after the measurable representation has been constructed.

Breakdown.Cert.testDenseHolds_proof.text: Equation (7.3) presents a tensor testing family. The formal result proves separation by periodized compact space-time tests, so it expresses the needed density property through a different testing description.

Breakdown.Cert.testPairingHolds_proof.text: The paper uses physical space-time pairings. This row identifies those pairings with the projected Fourier inner product against compact solenoidal tests, under the representation hypotheses used by the certificate argument.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationC.text: Equation (B.26) gives a finite quadratic comparison on reconstructed cell vectors. The formal condition requires that comparison on a specified admissible row domain and adds positivity, slack and boundedness conditions; connecting that domain to physical reconstruction uses row and gauge identities.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange.text: Equation (B.26) writes the reconstructed vector as $x=X_Qx_g$. The formal domain also allows complex gauge and head contributions and requires the two actuator blocks to be real, so the identification needs the accompanying row and gauge results.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.Internal.Rem.text: Equation (C.1) uses the curl-cross form of the continuum equation. This row supplies a vector-calculus identity relating that form to convection and a gradient term; it says nothing about the numerical search procedure.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.remainderAnn.text: Equation (C.2) gives the linearized continuum coupling. The formal theorem establishes the corresponding orthogonality under weak testing with explicit derivative, pressure and actuator data; the numerical Newton and iterative linear solves remain separate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsModeClass.text: The paper’s symmetry class in (B.1) has a twisted half-period rotation and a reflection. This condition requires those two generators and azimuthal order at least one; the full cell hypothesis separately raises the order to at least three and controls the generated symmetry family.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.modeShiftRotat.text: The formal transformation has the phase and rotated components of (B.13). Its periodicity and orbit-integrability hypotheses hold for the perturbations used in the cell argument.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsStrong.text: Equation (C.2) describes the linearized curl-cross equation. This condition specifies its physical right side with explicit pressure and actuator terms; it is a continuum hypothesis and does not verify the numerical solver.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.coupling.text: The formal coupling contains the two curl-cross terms of (C.2), with the background and perturbation in the two orders. Its weak-testing identities and the numerical solver are separate steps.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellHypothesis.text: The full cell hypothesis includes the two symmetries of (B.1), azimuthal order at least three, and the stated fixed weight, coercivity and pin coefficients. The separate symmetry condition alone imposes the lower order bound one.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.field.text: Equation (B.10) forms the same pin tensor and gradient pairing. The formal matrix representation orders output before input, so translating the displayed matrix requires the corresponding transpose convention.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesPiv.text: The tree test requires pivot coverage, positive slack, a nonnegative root form and an upper bound on the number of negative columns. These are hypotheses for the positivity conclusion, as described in the passage.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFiel.text: The finite sum in (B.6) is assembled from single harmonic contributions. For valid conjugate-closed coefficients, taking the real part gives the same real field; the coefficient symmetry conditions remain required.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.chartCoord.text: For positive chart length, the compactified radius is |y|/(|y|+L) as in (B.3). The formal arithmetic also defines endpoint and origin values, whose regularity is established using the shape conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.phaseSlope.text: The formal phase factor and radial differential expression reproduce (B.5): σ(1−σ)∂σ is supplemented by the phase-index term involving the radial phase slope.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowInstanc.text: Equation (B.11) places the row weight in the field normalization. The formal rows have unit norm and keep the factor τₖ in a separate weight equal to the test weight divided by coercivity; the weighted seminorm agrees after this translation.

Breakdown.CertCell.InstanceSplit.Enclosu.text: The three enclosure inequalities in (B.19) appear explicitly as required inequalities. This condition assumes them for the supplied data and performs no numerical enclosure calculation.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.fieldPairin.text: For (B.11), the formal Gram matrix pairs the real row generators before normalization. The separate row weights carry the factors that the paper places in its weighted rows.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.mix.text: For (B.11), the formal mixing matrix is the inverse square root of the Hermitian Gram matrix. It produces unit-norm rows when the Gram positivity hypotheses hold, while the paper’s τₖ factors remain in separate row weights.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.rowWeightOf.text: The formal row weight is the test weight divided by coercivity. This gives the factor used in (B.11) after separating it from the unit-norm row field, so weighting both the field and the coefficient would count it twice.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsDirectionR.text: Lemma B.6 permits the stated ray exteriors. This formal condition specifies a measurable homogeneous radial function with one strictly positive lower bound and a common upper bound; the exterior integral estimate is a separate result.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.Pa.text: The formal point test is exactly the conjunction of the four inequalities in (B.29), using the adjusted gradient floor and shifted velocity coefficient.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.gr.text: The formal gradient floor is the adjusted coefficient f₁* in (B.29). The other three inequalities enter the separate point-test condition.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget.H.text: The full formal tail comparison uses the Hessian gain with degree shift two and the same axis/off-axis radial threshold as (B.27). It compares all required curl, strain and velocity charges.

Breakdown.CertCell.cellFormAssembly_clos.text: Proposition B.4 presents the cell conclusion using four correction terms. The formal cell assembly distributes it among row, gauge, stretching, tail and reconstruction estimates under explicit data conditions, so this row is a component of that reconstruction.

Breakdown.CertCell.cellLayerParts_closed.text: The formal theorem supplies the analytic cell estimates used to reconstruct Proposition B.4. Applying them still requires the finite entry conditions, and the theorem supplies no particular numerical entries.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelHarmonic.text: In (B.2), the label (ι₁,ι₂) gives frequencies (2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁). The formal label map is exactly this arithmetic conversion.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase.text: The phase is exp(i(2π(2ι₂−ι₁)t+κι₁θ)), matching (B.2) after the common period-one time convention is used.

Breakdown.CertCell.stateEnclosureCertifi.text: Proposition B.8 combines finiteness with the global inequality (B.21). This row proves the signed tree positivity component; the later cell remainder estimate supplies the full endpoint under the shape, cell and entry conditions.

Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointQuadratic.text: Lemma B.10 permits either an L³-based or an L²-based sufficient norm bound. The formal condition makes that same choice and uses the corresponding coefficient before integration over one period.

Breakdown.CertReduction.EnergyBoundsHold.text: Equation (B.46) lists several estimates for a general weight. The formal package supplies squared weak-field and period-integrated versions at a constant positive weight, so its scope and arrangement differ from the full displayed family.

Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadCoeff.text: The formal coefficient chooses between the same L³-based and L²-based constants as Lemma B.10. The choice must agree with the norm bound used for the adjoint.

Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadratic.text: For the fixed cell adjoint, the formal conclusion is the quadratic pairing estimate of Lemma B.10 with the same two sufficient norm choices. The general statement additionally permits the selected adjoint to depend on the parameter.

Breakdown.CertReduction.cubicWeightProdu.text: The cubic product estimate is the squared form of the $2/\sqrt{3}$ factor used in (B.49): its coefficient is $4/3$. Together with the uniform and gradient alternatives it supplies the stated shift estimates.

Breakdown.CertReduction.formShiftBridgeH.text: Lemma B.9 separates the model-to-profile gap and the change of the frozen quadratic form. This row gives the form-shift estimate, using the same piecewise derivative choices and constants.

Breakdown.CertReduction.frozenFormBridge.text: For Lemma B.9, the formal result turns the model-form bound into the frozen convection bound using the integration-by-parts identity. Gap transfer and profile change are separate implications.

Breakdown.CertReduction.gapGradTermHolds.text: The formal gradient contribution in (B.49) uses the selected L² or L³ piece estimate with its corresponding coefficient. Its period square bound feeds the gap-transfer inequality.

Breakdown.CertReduction.gapSupTermHolds_.text: The uniform contribution in (B.49) has coefficient $s/\sqrt{w_0}$, or its square for the squared period norm. The formal statement retains the positive constant weight and perturbation hypotheses.

Breakdown.CertReduction.gapTransferBridg.text: This formal result is the gap-transfer part of Lemma B.9. It combines the uniform and gradient contributions of the prescribed profile-minus-model pieces.

Breakdown.Coercive.Internal.TestDensityP.text: Equation (C.1) uses the identity −Δv=curl curl v for divergence-free v. The formal row proves that vector-calculus step under the test-field assumptions, without addressing the numerical computation surrounding the equation.

Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.ExtendedCoerciveC.text: The coercivity conclusion quantifies over every admissible perturbation, multiplier and square-integrable right side. It therefore has the same continuum scope stated in the passage, beyond any finite trial family.

Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.IsAdmissibleWeak.text: Proposition B.1 assumes admissible weights and a background field. This formal condition spells out the weight, coefficient and regularity requirements for a background with a specified weak Hessian; it is the input to the multiplier-existence result.

Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.PieceMultiplierDe.text: The formal result gives multiplier existence, seminorm finiteness, its energy bound and a comparison of nonnegative density integrals. A finite negative density then permits subtraction to obtain the real signed-integral conclusion in Proposition B.1.

Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveC.text: The formal reduction combines the two signed density comparisons and the c₁,c₂ budgets to give Lemma B.2. The perturbations are represented using weak first and second derivatives.

Breakdown.DiscreteDichotomyStatement.text: Lemma 4.6 writes a specific weighted forced recurrence. The formal result gives a bounded solution of an equivalent discrete recurrence after a suitable exceptional initial component is chosen; its variables and piecewise scaling differ.

Breakdown.EmbeddedProfileOrbit.text: For Proposition 4.1, the formal statement retains the literal embedding of the supplied profile as its recurrent orbit. It uses the formal profile’s derivative and pressure decay hypotheses, which are more explicit than the printed proposition.

Breakdown.FarField.BilinKernel.text: Equation (3.10) permits arbitrary tensor divergences and distinct inputs. The formal formula here gives the diagonal bilinear convolution for a general Fourier state, with almost-everywhere physical equality.

Breakdown.FarField.BilinTestKernel.text: Equation (3.10) permits arbitrary tensor divergences and distinct inputs. This formal formula treats the diagonal convolution of a smooth compactly supported solenoidal test field.

Breakdown.FarField.LerayKernelBound.text: Equation (3.9) bounds every derivative order of the Oseen tensor. The formal statement here is the power-four parabolic bound for the kernel of the Leray-projected divergence, which is the specific derivative used later.

Breakdown.FarField.bilinKernel_of_test_d.text: The formal theorem extends the diagonal physical convolution formula from compact solenoidal tests to general Fourier states. Equation (3.10) presents the broader tensor and two-input identity.

Breakdown.FarField.farFieldDecay_holds.text: For the smooth orbit field satisfying the profile integral equation, the formal conclusion gives velocity derivatives of orders zero, one and two with decay powers one, two and three, and cubic pressure-gradient decay. These are the decay powers used in the passage.

Breakdown.FarField.integralEquationOfOrb.text: The paper’s profile equation is represented here by an integral from the infinite past for the chosen smooth orbit field. The formal theorem assumes the physical convolution and orbit-decay facts used to justify this representation.

Breakdown.FarField.lerayKernel.text: The formal definition is the kernel of the Leray-projected divergence. Equation (3.9) concerns all derivatives of the Oseen tensor; the later kernel bound supplies the power-four case used here.

Breakdown.FarField.lerayKernelBound_hold.text: The formal theorem proves power-four parabolic decay for the Leray-divergence kernel. Equation (3.9) states the wider family of Oseen-tensor derivative bounds.

Breakdown.Freq.BilinBound.text: The formal estimate bounds the bilinear term by $C\tau^{-3/4}\|u\|\|v\|$. Lemma 3.1 also includes a general $L^{3/2}$-forcing assertion, which is not a conclusion of this row.

Breakdown.Freq.BilinCompact.text: Lemma 3.2 allows every fixed element of X. The formal statement shown here assumes that fixed element belongs to the dense span of smooth compactly supported solenoidal fields, so its stated domain is narrower.

Breakdown.Freq.DilationAlgebra.text: The formal dilation laws give the norm factor $\mu^{1/4}$, composition of positive scales, and the heat intertwining identity of (3.5).

Breakdown.Freq.GradSixDecay.text: The Sobolev estimate in (3.1) is represented here first for smooth decaying fields. The continuous velocity map extends it to the completed Fourier space in a separate step.

Breakdown.Freq.HeatSemigroup.text: The formal heat evolution has the Fourier multiplier, semigroup law, contraction and strong continuity of (3.3), together with self-adjointness.

Breakdown.Freq.MildOfWeak.text: Lemma 3.6 gives a weak-to-mild implication. The formal version additionally requires smooth decaying slices and L²-continuity of their differences, which are supplied for the smooth profile route.

Breakdown.Freq.VelocityDilate.text: Equation (7.63) displays rescaled physical fields and their suprema. This formal statement gives almost-everywhere covariance of recovered velocity under dilation; the supremum identity requires the later choice of representative.

Breakdown.Freq.partial_holds.text: Equation (3.2) describes the Fourier realization of the gradient norm. The formal theorem recovers the three physical derivatives almost everywhere and bounds their squared norms for the gradient-weighted Fourier representation.

Breakdown.Freq.velocityCov_holds.text: Equation (7.63) displays rescaled physical fields and their suprema. The formal theorem gives almost-everywhere rotation and dilation identities for recovered velocity; it does not state the displayed supremum equality.

Breakdown.MildFramework.selfSimilar.text: The formal self-similar field is normalized to final time one and uses a freely chosen similarity-time phase. Formula (1.4) permits an arbitrary final time T.

Breakdown.MonodromyStatement.text: Lemma 3.4 treats the linear Volterra problem on an interval. The formal period-map argument inverts operators on sufficiently short pieces and then composes them, so the stated intermediate conclusion is different.

Breakdown.Periodic.ApproxFieldProperties.text: Lemma 5.1 is expressed using a large spatial cutoff scale. The formal result uses a fixed cutoff around the centre of the unit torus and a small time scale, and states smoothness, support, divergence freedom and agreement in the inner ball.

Breakdown.Periodic.ApproxResidualSmall.text: Lemma 6.2 presents the approximation in the paper’s spatial-scale variables. The formal residual estimate is for normalized time pieces and has bound $\theta^nKT^{1/4}$, with the unit-torus scaling retained.

Breakdown.Periodic.ApproxSizes.text: Lemma 6.2 presents the approximation in the paper’s spatial-scale variables. The formal size statement gives uniform upper and strictly positive lower bounds for the normalized pieces at sufficiently small T.

Breakdown.Periodic.ComparisonSmall.text: Lemma 6.3 gives an explicit candidate and an $L^{-1/2}$ defect bound. The formal comparison gives arbitrarily small operator error once the scale is small enough; the right-inverse transfer is a separate exact implication.

Breakdown.Periodic.FreeHeatComparison.text: The formal free-heat comparison converges uniformly over a bounded time window for each compact solenoidal test field as the scale tends to zero. Equation (6.3) additionally displays a rate in the spatial parameter L.

Breakdown.Periodic.GlueUnbounded.text: Formula (1.7) gives a local quantitative blow-up estimate. The formal conclusion shown here is unboundedness of the glued solution norm before its terminal time, without that local estimate or rate.

Breakdown.Periodic.HeatDivFreeComparison.text: Lemma 6.1 gives a uniform quantitative heat comparison. This formal statement gives arbitrarily small error on positive-time windows for compactly supported $L^2$ forcing, with an $L^{3/2}$ norm on the right side.

Breakdown.Periodic.KernelSharpBound.text: Lemma 3.7 treats periodic forcing for general spatial periods. The formal kernel bound is on the unit torus with its inhomogeneous norm for 0<τ≤1; rescaling is handled elsewhere.

Breakdown.Periodic.RightInversePerturb.text: Equation (6.16) chooses scales to satisfy three named inequalities. This formal perturbation lemma instead starts with an existing right inverse and requires ‖A′−A‖K≤1/2, yielding a right inverse bounded by 2K.

Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation.text: Lemma 4.8 works in a weighted curve space. The formal contraction theorem works with rescaled sequences of pieces and explicit residual and initial-data smallness, preserving the same perturbative purpose with different variables.

Breakdown.Periodic.ShellInverseTransfer.text: Lemma 6.3 gives a scale-dependent construction of the periodic inverse. This formal theorem transfers a right inverse between two shell decompositions under exact norm and comparison hypotheses; the small-scale estimates are separate inputs.

Breakdown.Periodic.ShellTorus.Internal.s.text: For (3.19), the formal theorem bounds compactly supported L² forcing after transplantation to the unit torus, with μτ≤1 and its inhomogeneous norm. The paper permits all positive times and periods in a mean-zero homogeneous space.

Breakdown.Periodic.TransplantNorm.text: Equation (6.1) is a homogeneous norm identity. The formal unit-torus transplantation identity includes the additional term μ‖g‖²₂, reflecting its inhomogeneous norm.

Breakdown.Periodic.sourceOp.text: The formal definition supplies the transplanted unit-torus forcing operator used in the restricted estimate near (3.19). Its $L^{3/2}$ bound and the short-time condition $\mu\tau\le 1$ are established separately.

Breakdown.Periodic.trigHs.text: The formal Sobolev estimate treats finite Fourier polynomials on the unit cell with an inhomogeneous weight. Equation (3.18) states a homogeneous inequality uniform over the spatial period.

Breakdown.PeriodicInverseStatement.text: Proposition 4.3 solves the problem in a global weighted curve space. The formal construction uses bounded sequences of short rescaled pieces, a finite-dimensional correction and a lift into the chosen dense data space.

Breakdown.PhysicalMild.text: For Proposition 4.1, the formal statement makes the embedded physical field mild on each closed interval before time one. It assumes the smooth profile’s derivative and pressure decay bounds and continuity of its embedding.

Breakdown.PhysicalWeak.text: Equation (3.14) is the weak momentum identity after the pressure term is removed by solenoidal testing. The formal expression uses gradient and advection pairings under the stronger decay and regularity conditions of the supplied profile.

Breakdown.PieceOperatorStatement.text: Lemma 4.7 gives three estimates in a weighted curve space. The formal statement treats the bilinear and free operators on a compact time piece; global time weights are handled in the later sequence construction.

Breakdown.PiecePerturbationStatement.text: Equation (4.7) states an equivalence over the whole lifespan. The formal result gives the forward implication on a compact piece: a solution of the correction equation yields the prescribed initial correction and a mild corrected background.

Breakdown.ProfilePieceStatement.text: Lemma 4.2 gives a physical-time description of the rescaled trajectory. The formal statement gives the corresponding recurrent pieces and their uniform bounds; the physical rate follows after the dilation norm law is applied.

Breakdown.StepDataStatement.text: Proposition 4.3 solves the linearized problem in a weighted curve space. The formal construction chooses the number of pieces, a sequence weight, a finite-dimensional correction and a bounded recurrence solver, with the dense initial-data lift retained.

Breakdown.UniqueStatement.text: The formal row gives uniqueness of quadratic mild solutions on both closed and half-open intervals. The paper’s Lemma 3.5 also contains a restart assertion for separate input curves, which is outside this row’s conclusion.

Breakdown.VarConstIntegralStatement.text: Lemma 3.3 is stated on the paper’s time interval. The formal result gives integrability and continuity on every compact interval and, for $t-a\le 1$, the explicit bound $4C_K(t-a)^{1/4}MN$.

Breakdown.WeakProfile.mildFromGood_holds.text: The formal result gives the same heat evolution plus bilinear time integral as (7.64), in the completed Fourier space. The physical kernel identification is supplied by the corresponding representation results.

Breakdown.WeakProfile.physicalIdentity_o.text: Equation (7.41) displays the pointwise change-of-variable identities. The formal result establishes the transformed weak equation against rescaled tests, which is the integrated conclusion needed for the weak-profile route.

Breakdown.profilePiece.text: Lemma 4.2 describes the recurrent rescaled pieces in physical variables. The formal theorem proves their mild equation, matching endpoints, recurrence and norm bound; the physical-time rate follows from the dilation law.

families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).
